text.title: Library Evaluation Rubric Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on how many candidates are genuinely choosable, on the cost of reversing the choice (import sites, type leakage), and on whether the dependency ships in the artefact — to the full rubric, a reduced build-time rubric, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there more than one viable candidate the operator is actually free to choose between?

conclusion.verdict: skip; record a one-line ADR naming the single option — a scored table would lend a forced choice authority the evidence never supported

branch.question: What does reversing the choice cost — how many import sites are projected, and do the library's types leak into your public API signatures or persisted data?

conclusion.verdict: skip; the swap is cheaper than the evaluation — adopt, and revisit if import sites grow

branch.question: Does the dependency ship in the runtime artefact (client bundle or distributed binary), or is it build-time-only?

conclusion.verdict: apply a reduced rubric — maintenance signals, time-to-patch, transitive count and install-script surface; bundle-delta and distribution-licence criteria do not apply
apply the full rubric: bundle delta measured on the real import path, transitive licence scan, time-to-patch history, and an adapter bounding exit cost above 10 import sites
